batchName: Middle Republic: Rome Turns East (200-167 BCE) - Latin words
chapterName: Middle Republic: Rome Turns East (200-167 BCE)
description: Written by hand from the chapter text: the Latin words it explains

questions.question: At the Isthmian Games of 196 BC, Flamininus proclaimed libertas for the Greeks. What does it mean?
questions.explanation: The crowd erupted in joy, though Rome kept troops in the “fetters of Greece”.
questions.sourceQuote: the Roman commander Flamininus proclaimed freedom (*libertas*) for the Greek communities Philip had ruled.

questions.question: In 171 BC Rome declared Perseus a hostis. What was that?
questions.explanation: Rome had heard the king of Pergamon accuse him of preparing for war.
questions.sourceQuote: Rome declared him a public enemy (*hostis*), and war began in 171 BC.

questions.question: How did Aemilius Paullus celebrate his victory over Perseus?
options: With a triumphus, Perseus led in chains before it
By building a temple at Pydna
By freeing all the Macedonian prisoners
questions.explanation: Perseus spent the rest of his life under guard at Alba Fucens, in central Italy.
questions.sourceQuote: celebrated a triumph (*triumphus*), the grand victory parade, with Perseus led in chains before it.

questions.question: Under the Peace of Apamea, Antiochus sent twenty obsides to Rome. Who were they?
questions.explanation: He also had to hand over Rome’s enemies, but Hannibal fled instead.
questions.sourceQuote: Twenty hostages (*obsides*), including his youngest son, went to Rome

questions.question: How much tributum did each of the four Macedonian republics pay Rome?
options: Half what the king had taken
Twice what the king had taken
The same as under the king
questions.explanation: Rome declared the Macedonians free but dismantled their kingdom.
questions.sourceQuote: each paying Rome a tribute (*tributum*) half what the king had taken.

questions.question: Which Roman assembly voted unanimously for peace with Philip V in 197 BC?
questions.explanation: Philip had to withdraw his garrisons, pay 1,000 talents and give up his navy.
questions.sourceQuote: the Tribal Assembly (*comitia tributa*), another of the citizen assemblies, voted unanimously for it.

questions.question: What happened when a consul first asked the comitia centuriata to declare war on Philip V in 200 BC?
options: It voted for war at once
It asked the Senate to decide
It voted to make peace with Carthage
questions.explanation: The refusal was blamed on exhaustion; at a second meeting the consul changed their minds.
questions.sourceQuote: In 200 BC one of the consuls asked the Centuriate Assembly (*comitia centuriata*), the citizen body that alone could declare war, to vote for war.

questions.question: Why did Flamininus care whether his command got a prorogatio?
options: If replaced, he wanted the credit for a quick peace
He wanted to become consul again at once
He hoped to be sent to Spain
He wanted to retire to Greece
questions.explanation: Once he learned his command was extended, his friends in Rome quietly sank the peace talks.
questions.sourceQuote: Flamininus did not yet know whether his command would be extended (*prorogatio*).
